strengths: Technically sound methodology with edge-conditioned transformer and aligned functional gradients providing principled inductive bias for dense brain graphs
Comprehensive experimental validation across HCP (N=1067) and BSNIP (n=984) datasets with proper train/val/test splits and careful data leakage prevention
Thorough ablations (Table 2) and multiple complementary evaluation metrics (reconstruction, classification, distribution alignment) demonstrating each component's contribution

Novel combination of techniques addressing genuine problem (avoiding thresholding artifacts in FC graphs) with domain-specific innovations (Procrustes-aligned gradients, memory-based cross-attention decoder)
Unsupervised learning of representations that meaningfully separate cognitive states and enable downstream decoding without label supervision
Well-designed extensions (neural dynamics fusion improves cognitive decoding to 89.7%, latent diffusion enables graph generation) that validate interpretability of learned geometry
Transparent presentation with detailed hyperparameters, ablations, and honest limitations discussion; code availability promised
Neuroscientifically meaningful insights linking gradient-related latent reconfiguration to behavioral performance while demonstrating that excessive task-evoked dispersion is detrimental
weaknesses: Empirical improvements over baselines are modest (~22% reconstruction improvement over GATE, 78.6% cognitive load classification, 73.7% AUC for HC vs schizophrenia) and clinical significance remains unclear

Limited architectural novelty: edge-conditioned attention from Ma et al. (2023), functional gradients from Margulies et al. (2016), Procrustes alignment and diffusion models established; primary contribution is engineering combination rather than introducing fundamentally new concepts

Inconsistent application of gradient geometry: 20% sparsification used for gradient computation but dense FC for reconstruction objective—rationale unclear and potentially introduces bias in inductive bias

Interpretability limited: two-factor latent readout explains only R²=0.52 of variance in network metrics (Δ²={0.38, 0.14}), leaving substantial unexplained variance; no systematic probing of learned latent structure
Gradient spread proxy (Eq. 7) using range is susceptible to outliers despite post-hoc quantile robustness check; no ablation on alternative measures

Diffusion generation validation incomplete: no evaluation of neurobiological plausibility of generated graphs or validation that synthetic samples preserve known connectomic properties beyond summary statistics
Limited baseline comparisons: no simple dimensionality reduction baselines (PCA/ICA on graphs), no VAE graph autoencoders; missing 2024 work besides GRALE

Paper covers too many topics (representation, generation, cognitive decoding, interpretation) creating somewhat diffuse narrative; connections between three extensions feel disconnected rather than integrated

Experimental design limitations: only 4 random seeds, working-memory analysis uses specific partitioning with unclear generalizability, no sensitivity analysis to resting-state template choice, classification uses only logistic regression

Statistical reporting inconsistencies: task dispersion effect (β=-0.16) is statistically significant but effect size small; some results lack confidence intervals; multiple comparisons corrections not always explicit
Clinical applicability unvalidated: BSNIP results positioned as research tools only; no comparison to conventional clinical markers, no treatment-naive vs treated analysis, no longitudinal validation
Missing analyses: no cross-site validation, no robustness assessment to preprocessing variations, no investigation of why edge-conditioned attention outperforms sparse attention for this domain

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing dense functional connectivity representation with clear articulation of limitations in sparse thresholding and node-level approaches
Comprehensive experimental validation with large-scale datasets (HCP N=1067, BSNIP N=984), careful subject-wise splits preventing data leakage, and thorough ablation studies
Thoughtful architectural choices including edge-conditioned attention for dense graphs and memory-based cross-attention decoder with clear domain-informed reasoning
Extensive appendix with detailed hyperparameters, training protocols, multiple baseline comparisons (GAE, Graphite, GRALE, GATE), and ablations across different parcellations
Multi-faceted evaluation across reconstruction, cognitive decoding, generation, and latent space interpretation
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty for a top-tier ML venue: edge-conditioned attention from Ma et al. (2023), standard diffusion models from Ho et al. (2020), and memory-based cross-attention are existing techniques; core contribution reduces to their application with functional gradients as node features

Unclear necessity and mechanism of functional gradients: only ~23% improvement over edge-only baseline and marginal advantage over graph-theoretic features (0.0124 vs 0.0153); ablation lacks systematic comparison with alternative node feature sets to isolate gradient contribution
Modest empirical improvements insufficient for ICML: reconstruction MSE 0.0124 vs 0.0143-0.0155 for baselines (~20% relative gain); no statistical significance testing of these differences

Weak downstream validation: cognitive decoding achieves 78.6% (0-back vs 2-back) and 60-64% (stimulus categories) without comparison to supervised methods or other unsupervised approaches; generation validated only via distributional metrics (KS=0.129 for eigenvalues indicates notable mismatch); no assessment of generative utility for downstream analysis

Severe practical limitations: works only for fixed-region-level parcellations with quadratic attention cost preventing higher resolutions; gradient computation depends on specific preprocessing and template alignment; generalization across sites, protocols, and atlases untested despite acknowledged importance

Cognitive-neuroscience analysis lacks depth: task-dispersion correlation β=-0.16 and PC2-cognition r=0.23 indicate weak effect sizes; findings are purely correlational without mechanistic understanding; detailed analysis limited to working memory despite claiming 7-task analysis

Unfocused scope attempting four distinct contributions (representation learning, cognitive decoding, generation, interpretation) with insufficient depth in any; spatial-temporal improvement not properly ablated to separate temporal information from geometric fusion contributions

Methodological concerns: dense MSE loss equally weights edges without confidence consideration; top-20% sparsification used for gradients but not for main FC representation (inconsistent); memory mechanism initialization and some architectural choices (e.g., ρ(x) function) lack justification

Statistical rigor issues: extremely small standard deviations (±0.0006) without significance tests; multiple comparisons without systematic correction; diffusion generation validated on only 50 samples; no investigation of statistical significance in reconstruction differences

Ethics statement vague on privacy mitigation (beyond de-identification); no fairness analysis across demographics; substantial discussion of limitations but positioned as future work rather than addressing current validity

strengths: Well-motivated integration of aligned functional gradients as domain-specific inductive bias for dense graph learning, grounded in neuroscience literature
Rigorous experimental validation across multiple datasets (HCP N=1067, BSNIP N=984) with proper data leakage prevention and comprehensive ablations
Comprehensive framework unifying representation learning, generation, and interpretation; unsupervised embeddings enable cognitive decoding (up to 89.7% with dynamics)
Superior reconstruction of dense FC without thresholding (MSE 0.0124±0.0006) vs. multiple baselines while preserving both topological and spectral properties
Excellent presentation with clear figures, detailed methods, thorough appendix, and honest limitations discussion; good reproducibility documentation
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty: individual components (graph transformers, edge conditioning, diffusion models, functional gradients) are established; novelty lies primarily in combination and application

Key design choices lack full justification: (1) hybrid sparsification for gradients but dense learning, (2) edge stabilization function ρ(x), (3) equal loss weighting in neural dynamics, (4) substantial jump in gradient dimensionality (F=10 to F=30)
Cognitive analysis shows modest effect sizes: cross-task dispersion-cognition r=0.23, PC2-cognition β=0.23, mechanistic interpretation is post-hoc and underdeveloped
Generation validation incomplete: distribution alignment shown but utility of generated graphs for downstream analysis not demonstrated; diffusion convergence/sensitivity not analyzed

Scope limitations reduce broader impact: requires fixed parcellations with consistent node ordering, quadratic complexity prevents voxel-level extension, positioned as research tools requiring external validation

Implementation details missing: code availability link appears blank in submission, no sensitivity analysis for several hyperparameters (diffusion epochs, RNN latent dimension r=8, memory mechanism regularization)
